newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels say they seized garrisons in east.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say they seized garrisons in east.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Thursday they had captured three army garrisons in eastern Sudan north of the city of Kassala after offensives in the northeast and south.
Yassir Arman, spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), said rebels captured Koteneb and Gedemayeeb garrisons 100 km (60 miles) north of Kassala on Wednesday.

Bakheet Ali al-Hassan, Eritrea representative for the Sudan Alliance Forces, said the rebels also captured Tokan garrison on Wednesday night. All three garrisons are in the same area and about 40 km (25 miles) from Sudan's border with Eritrea.
The SPLA are grouped with other movements in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA), which attacked in the east in January and launched offensives in the south and northeast last month.
Arman said NDA deputy chairman General Fathi Ahmed Ali and SPLA leader John Garang addressed more than 1,000 prisoners of war in Western Equatoria region in Sudan's south on Wednesday.
Since 1983 the SPLA has fought for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. The NDA says it aims to trigger a popular uprising in Khartoum.
